title: Working-capital loans pushed up Taiwan’s five-bank new lending rate in October
bank: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
summary: The average rate charged on new loans by five large Taiwanese banks rose from 2.193% in September to 2.254% in October. The central bank attributes the increase to the rate on loans for current operations. The annex explains why that category can move the headline even as other rates fall. These banks originated NT$975.1 billion of current-operations loans in October, about 83% of the NT$1.172 trillion total for the four loan purposes shown. Their average rate rose from 2.160% to 2.236%, a 7.6 basis point increase on a large share of new business.

The category had an even larger weight in September: NT$1.156 trillion out of NT$1.326 trillion. A calculation from the annex helps separate pricing and composition. Holding September’s volume weights constant, the change in the rate on current-operations loans alone added about 6.6 basis points to the overall average. Lower rates on the other types of borrowing partly offset that contribution, most visibly the 13.4 basis point fall for capital expenditure loans. Across all four categories, applying October rates to September weights gives a 5.7 basis point increase. Shifting to October weights at October rates adds about 0.4 basis point. Within-category changes in the mix of borrowers can still affect the first component. This calculation uses the rounded amounts and rates in the official sheet.

The amount advanced and the rate charged moved in opposite directions for current-operations loans. New lending in that category fell by about NT$181.2 billion from September, while new capital expenditure loans rose about NT$24.0 billion and new housing loans about NT$3.0 billion. The average new housing loan rate edged down from 2.315% to 2.312%. For an investor following household borrowing costs, the 6.1 basis point increase in the headline would therefore give the wrong direction for new housing loans in this sample. The average on new consumer loans also declined. The annex also reports a base lending rate of 3.265% in both months. A stable reference rate therefore coexisted with changes in transaction rates and in the amounts originated at those rates. The table supplies no borrower-level margins over that reference rate, which would be needed to identify a change in negotiated spreads.

The treatment of Treasury borrowings makes another material difference. Excluding them, the average rose from 2.214% to 2.258%, or 4.4 basis points. Including them, it was lower in both months and showed a larger monthly increase. The release gives both versions so readers can assess how official-sector borrowing affects the aggregate. It gives no breakdown of loan maturities, collateral or borrower credit quality within each purpose. A higher rate on new current-operations business can reflect a change in which borrowers took out loans as well as a change in the terms offered to comparable applicants.

The publication covers five named domestic banks and newly originated loans. The annex identifies an earlier change in bank membership in 2008, relevant to long historical comparisons. The series does not measure the average cost of the entire outstanding Taiwanese loan book or the date on which existing borrowers reprice. Balance-sheet exposure to this month’s change depends on banks’ product and borrower mix, the amount of new business and how quickly existing contracts reset.

questions.question: Was current-operations credit repriced for comparable firms?
questions.detail: The weighted rate rose 7.6 basis points while origination volume fell markedly. A change in borrower size, maturity or risk could alter the weighted rate even if posted pricing barely moved. Compare successive releases with bank-level data on matched borrower groups, tenor and collateral where available. Persistent increases within those groups would provide stronger evidence of tightening financing conditions for firms.

questions.question: How much of the aggregate movement comes from Treasury borrowing?
questions.detail: The increase excluding the Treasury was 4.4 basis points, against 6.1 including it. The annex shows the difference in aggregate rates without identifying a Treasury borrowing schedule or the rates on individual loans. Check public borrowing calendars, amounts and actual borrowing terms alongside future five-bank releases. This matters when using the headline series to infer pricing of private credit.

questions.question: When would these new-loan rates affect borrowers’ interest bills and bank income?
questions.detail: The October table concerns newly extended loans and separates four purposes. It gives no repricing dates for outstanding exposures. Match new-business volumes to outstanding balances, floating-rate shares and reset schedules by product. For lenders, also examine deposit and other funding costs. A change in the price of one month’s originations alone cannot identify the movement in net interest margins.
